name: Do drywall repair patches need primer before touching up paint?

mainEntity.name: Do drywall repair patches need primer before touching up paint?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drywall patches must always be sealed with a dedicated primer before applying wall paint. Unprimed joint compound absorbs paint differently than the surrounding painted paper face, causing a dull, discolored spot called paint flashing. Applying a quick-drying primer seals the porous mud, ensures consistent color absorption, and helps the finish sheen blend evenly with the rest of your wall.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, joint compound is porous and must be primed first; skipping primer causes the touched-up area to absorb paint unevenly and leave a dull, noticeable spot.
